sanskrit: tasya putrā maheṣvāsāḥ sarvaiḥ samuditā guṇaiḥ devayānyāṃ mahārāja śarmiṣṭhāyāṃ ca jajñire
english: His sons, mighty archers endowed with every virtue, O great king, were born of Devayānī and also of Śarmiṣṭhā.

sanskrit: devayānyām ajāyetāṃ yadus turvasur eva ca druhyuś cānuś ca pūruś ca śarmiṣṭhāyāṃ prajajñire
english: Yadu and Turvasu were born of Devayānī; and Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru were born of Śarmiṣṭhā.

sanskrit: sa śāśvatīḥ samā rājan prajā dharmeṇa pālayan jarām ārchan mahāghorāṃ nāhuṣo rūpanāśinīm
english: He, the son of Nahuṣa, ruled his people righteously through endless years, O king, while enduring a terrible old age that was destroying his beauty.

sanskrit: jarābhibhūtaḥ putrān sa rājā vacanam abravīt yaduṃ pūruṃ turvasuṃ ca druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca bhārata
english: Overwhelmed by old age, that king addressed his sons — Yadu, Pūru, Turvasu, Druhyu, and Anu — O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yauvanena caran kāmān yuvā yuvatibhiḥ saha vihartum aham icchāmi sāhyaṃ kuruta putrakāḥ
english: "I wish to roam in the pleasures of youth and to sport with young women as a young man — help me in this, my sons."

sanskrit: taṃ putro devayāneyaḥ pūrvajo yadur abravīt kiṃ kāryaṃ bhavataḥ kāryam asmābhir yauvanena ca
english: Then the elder son born of Devayānī, Yadu, said to him: "What is it that you need from us, and what use is our youth to you?"

sanskrit: yayātir abravīt taṃ vai jarā me pratigṛhyatām yauvanena tvadīyena careyaṃ viṣayān aham
english: Yayāti said to him: "Take my old age upon yourself; with your youth let me pursue the objects of pleasure."

sanskrit: yajato dīrghasatrair me śāpāc cośanaso muneḥ kāmārthaḥ parihīṇo me tapye 'haṃ tena putrakāḥ
english: "Through the curse of the sage Uśanas while I was performing long sacrificial sessions, I have been deprived of the fulfillment of desire, and I grieve because of it, my sons."

sanskrit: māmakena śarīreṇa rājyam ekaḥ praśāstu vaḥ ahaṃ tanvābhinavayā yuvā kāmān avāpnuyām
english: "Let one of you rule the kingdom with my body, while I, young in a fresh body, attain all pleasures."

sanskrit: na te tasya pratyagṛhṇan yaduprabhṛtayo jarām tam abravīt tataḥ pūruḥ kanīyān satyavikramaḥ
english: But Yadu and the others did not accept his old age. Then the youngest, Pūru, of true valor, spoke to him.

sanskrit: rājaṃś carābhinavayā tanvā yauvanagocaraḥ ahaṃ jarāṃ samāsthāya rājye sthāsyāmi te ''jñayā
english: "O king, roam in the realm of youth with a new body; I, having taken on old age, will remain in the kingdom by your command."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa rājarṣis tapovīryasamāśrayāt saṃcārayām āsa jarāṃ tadā putre mahātmani
english: Thus addressed, that royal sage, by the power of his ascetic vigor, transferred the old age then to his great-souled son.

sanskrit: pauraveṇātha vayasā rājā yauvanam āsthitaḥ yāyātenāpi vayasā rājyaṃ pūrur akārayat
english: Taking on the youth of the son of Pūru, the king entered into his prime; and bearing the age of Yayāti, Pūru governed the kingdom.

sanskrit: tato varṣasahasrānte yayātir aparājitaḥ atṛpta eva kāmānāṃ pūruṃ putram uvāca ha
english: Then, at the end of a thousand years, the unconquered Yayāti, still unsatiated in his desires, spoke to his son Pūru.

sanskrit: tvayā dāyādavān asmi tvaṃ me vaṃśakaraḥ sutaḥ pauravo vaṃśa iti te khyātiṃ loke gamiṣyati
english: "Through you I have obtained my inheritance; you are the son who carries on my lineage. The line of Pūru — by this name shall your fame go forth in the world."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa nṛpaśārdūlaḥ pūruṃ rājye 'bhiṣicya ca kālena mahatā paścāt kāladharmam upeyivān
english: Then that tiger among kings, having anointed Pūru to the kingdom, passed away to the law of time after a great span of years.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca yayātiḥ pūrvako 'smākaṃ daśamo yaḥ prajāpateḥ kathaṃ sa śukratanayāṃ lebhe paramadurlabhām
english: Janamejaya said: "Yayāti, our ancestor, who was the tenth from the Lord of Creatures — how did he obtain the daughter of Śukra, she who is supremely difficult to win?"

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ vistareṇa dvijottama ānupūrvyā ca me śaṃsa pūror vaṃśakarān pṛthak
english: "I wish to hear this in detail, O best of twice-born men; and in due order tell me separately of those who carried on the line of Pūru."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yayātir āsīd rājarṣir devarājasamadyutiḥ taṃ śukravṛṣaparvāṇau vavrāte vai yathā purā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Yayāti was a royal sage with the splendor equal to the king of gods. Both Śukra and Vṛṣaparvā chose him in affection in those ancient times."

sanskrit: tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi pṛcchato janamejaya devayānyāś ca saṃyogaṃ yayāter nāhuṣasya ca
english: "That I shall fully narrate to you as you ask, O Janamejaya — the union of Devayānī and of Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa."

sanskrit: surāṇām asurāṇāṃ ca samajāyata vai mithaḥ aiśvaryaṃ prati saṃgharṣas trailokye sacarācare
english: A conflict for supremacy arose between the gods and the demons, throughout the three worlds with all their moving and unmoving beings.

sanskrit: jigīṣayā tato devā vavrire ''ṅgirasaṃ munim paurohityena yājyārthe kāvyaṃ tūśanasaṃ pare brāhmaṇau tāv ubhau nityam anyonyaspardhinau bhṛśam
english: Desiring victory, the gods chose the sage Āṅgirasa as their chaplain and sacrificial priest; the others chose Uśanas Kāvya. Those two brahmins were always in fierce rivalry with each other.

sanskrit: tatra devā nijaghnur yān dānavān yudhi saṃgatān tān punar jīvayām āsa kāvyo vidyābalāśrayāt tatas te punar utthāya yodhayāṃ cakrire surān
english: There, whichever demons were slain by the gods in battle, Kāvya revived them again by resort to the power of his knowledge; and rising again, they fought the gods once more.

sanskrit: asurās tu nijaghnur yān surān samaramūrdhani na tān saṃjīvayām āsa bṛhaspatir udāradhīḥ
english: But those gods whom the demons slew in the thick of battle, Bṛhaspati of great intellect could not revive.

sanskrit: na hi veda sa tāṃ vidyāṃ yāṃ kāvyo veda vīryavān saṃjīvanīṃ tato devā viṣādam agaman param
english: For he did not know that knowledge — the life-restoring science — which the mighty Kāvya knew; and so the gods fell into the deepest despair.

sanskrit: te tu devā bhayodvignāḥ kāvyād uśanasas tadā ūcuḥ kacam upāgamya jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ bṛhaspateḥ
english: Then the gods, anxious with fear of Uśanas Kāvya, approached Kaca, the eldest son of Bṛhaspati, and spoke to him.

sanskrit: bhajamānān bhajasvāsmān kuru naḥ sāhyam uttamam yāsau vidyā nivasati brāhmaṇe 'mitatejasi śukre tām āhara kṣipraṃ bhāgabhāṅ no bhaviṣyasi
english: "Favor those who favor you; render us the highest help. That knowledge which resides in the brahmin Śukra of boundless splendor — quickly bring it forth, and you shall share in our portion."

sanskrit: vṛṣaparvasamīpe sa śakyo draṣṭuṃ tvayā dvijaḥ rakṣate dānavāṃs tatra na sa rakṣaty adānavān
english: "That twice-born one can be found near Vṛṣaparvā; there he protects the demons and does not protect non-demons."

sanskrit: tam ārādhayituṃ śakto bhavān pūrvavayāḥ kavim devayānīṃ ca dayitāṃ sutāṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "You, in the freshness of your youth, are capable of pleasing that sage, and also Devayānī, the beloved daughter of that great soul."

sanskrit: tvam ārādhayituṃ śakto nānyaḥ kaś cana vidyate śīladākṣiṇyamādhuryair ācāreṇa damena ca devayānyāṃ hi tuṣṭāyāṃ vidyāṃ tāṃ prāpsyasi dhruvam
english: "No one else exists who is capable of winning his favor — not through good conduct, courtesy, sweetness, right behavior, and self-restraint as you are. When Devayānī is pleased, you will surely obtain that knowledge."

sanskrit: tathety uktvā tataḥ prāyād bṛhaspatisutaḥ kacaḥ tadābhipūjito devaiḥ samīpaṃ vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
english: Saying "So be it," Kaca, the son of Bṛhaspati, then set out — duly honored by the gods — toward the dwelling of Vṛṣaparvā.

sanskrit: sa gatvā tvarito rājan devaiḥ saṃpreṣitaḥ kacaḥ asurendrapure śukraṃ dṛṣṭvā vākyam uvāca ha
english: Going swiftly, O king, sent forth by the gods, Kaca arrived at the city of the lord of demons, saw Śukra, and spoke these words.

sanskrit: ṛṣer aṅgirasaḥ pautraṃ putraṃ sākṣād bṛhaspateḥ nāmnā kaca iti khyātaṃ śiṣyaṃ gṛhṇātu māṃ bhavān
english: "Let your honor accept me as a pupil — the grandson of the sage Āṅgiras, the direct son of Bṛhaspati, known by the name Kaca."

sanskrit: brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyāmi tvayy ahaṃ paramaṃ gurau anumanyasva māṃ brahman sahasraṃ parivatsarān
english: "I shall practice the highest celibate studentship under you, the supreme teacher; grant me your approval, O brahmin, for a thousand years."

sanskrit: śukra uvāca kaca susvāgataṃ te 'stu pratigṛhṇāmi te vacaḥ arcayiṣye 'ham arcyaṃ tvām arcito 'stu bṛhaspatiḥ
english: Śukra said: "Kaca, be most welcome; I accept your words. I shall honor you who are worthy of honor, and may Bṛhaspati be honored through you."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kacas tu taṃ tathety uktvā pratijagrāha tad vratam ādiṣṭaṃ kaviputreṇa śukreṇośanasā svayam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Kaca, saying 'so be it,' accepted the vow that was prescribed by Śukra Uśanas, the son of the poet, himself."

sanskrit: vratasya vratakālaṃ sa yathoktaṃ pratyagṛhṇata ārādhayann upādhyāyaṃ devayānīṃ ca bhārata
english: He accepted the prescribed duration of the vow as directed, attending upon his teacher and Devayānī, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nityam ārādhayiṣyaṃs tāṃ yuvā yauvanago ''mukhe gāyan nṛtyan vādayaṃś ca devayānīm atoṣayat
english: Ever intent on pleasing her, that young man, at the threshold of youth, delighted Devayānī with singing, dancing, and playing music.

sanskrit: saṃśīlayan devayānīṃ kanyāṃ saṃprāptayauvanām puṣpaiḥ phalaiḥ preṣaṇaiś ca toṣayām āsa bhārata
english: Cultivating the company of Devayānī, the girl who had just come of age, he pleased her with flowers, fruits, and acts of service, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: devayāny api taṃ vipraṃ niyamavratacāriṇam anugāyamānā lalanā rahaḥ paryacarat tadā
english: And Devayānī too, that charming woman, singing along with him, attended upon that brahmin who practiced his vows and observances in private at that time.

sanskrit: pañca varṣaśatāny evaṃ kacasya carato vratam tatrātīyur atho buddhvā dānavās taṃ tataḥ kacam
english: Five hundred years passed thus while Kaca pursued his vow; then the demons, becoming aware of him, turned against Kaca.

sanskrit: gā rakṣantaṃ vane dṛṣṭvā rahasy ekam amarṣitāḥ jaghnur bṛhaspater dveṣād vidyārakṣārtham eva ca hatvā śālāvṛkebhyaś ca prāyacchaṃs tilaśaḥ kṛtam
english: Finding him alone in the forest tending the cows, in their rage and out of hatred for Bṛhaspati, and to protect the knowledge, they slew him; and having killed him, they ground him to sesame-sized pieces and fed him to wolves.

sanskrit: tato gāvo nivṛttās tā agopāḥ svaṃ niveśanam tā dṛṣṭvā rahitā gās tu kacenābhyāgatā vanāt uvāca vacanaṃ kāle devayāny atha bhārata
english: Then the cows returned to their fold without a cowherd. Seeing those cows come back from the forest without Kaca, Devayānī spoke these words at the right moment, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ahutaṃ cāgnihotraṃ te sūryaś cāstaṃ gataḥ prabho agopāś cāgatā gāvaḥ kacas tāta na dṛśyate
english: "Your fire-sacrifice has not been offered, and the sun has set, my lord; the cows have come back without a cowherd — father, Kaca is nowhere to be seen."

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ hato mṛto vāpi kacas tāta bhaviṣyati taṃ vinā na ca jīveyaṃ kacaṃ satyaṃ bravīmi te
english: "Clearly Kaca must have been slain or is dead, father; without him I cannot live — I tell you the truth."

sanskrit: śukra uvāca ayam ehīti śabdena mṛtaṃ saṃjīvayāmy aham
english: Śukra said: "By uttering the word 'come here,' I shall revive the dead."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ saṃjīvanīṃ vidyāṃ prayujya kacam āhvayat āhūtaḥ prādurabhavat kaco 'riṣṭo 'tha vidyayā hato 'ham iti cācakhyau pṛṣṭo brāhmaṇakanyayā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Employing the life-restoring knowledge, he called out to Kaca; summoned, Kaca appeared unharmed by virtue of that knowledge, and when questioned by the brahmin's daughter, he told her: 'I was slain.'"

sanskrit: sa punar devayānyoktaḥ puṣpāhāro yadṛcchayā vanaṃ yayau tato vipro dadṛśur dānavāś ca tam
english: Again, urged by Devayānī, the brahmin went to the forest at will to gather flowers; and the demons caught sight of him there.

sanskrit: tato dvitīyaṃ hatvā taṃ dagdhvā kṛtvā ca cūrṇaśaḥ prāyacchan brāhmaṇāyaiva surāyām asurās tadā
english: Then the demons slew him a second time, burned him, reduced him to powder, and mixed him into the wine of the brahmin himself.

sanskrit: devayāny atha bhūyo 'pi vākyaṃ pitaram abravīt puṣpāhāraḥ preṣaṇakṛt kacas tāta na dṛśyate
english: Again Devayānī spoke words to her father: "Kaca who went to gather flowers and run errands, father, is nowhere to be seen."

sanskrit: śukra uvāca bṛhaspateḥ sutaḥ putri kacaḥ pretagatiṃ gataḥ vidyayā jīvito 'py evaṃ hanyate karavāṇi kim
english: Śukra said: "Daughter, Bṛhaspati's son Kaca has gone the way of the dead. Though revived by the knowledge, he is slain again in this way — what can I do?"

sanskrit: maivaṃ śuco mā ruda devayāni; na tvādṛśī martyam anupraśocet surāś ca viśve ca jagac ca sarvam; upasthitāṃ vaikṛtim ānamanti
english: "Do not grieve thus, do not weep, Devayānī; one such as you should not mourn a mortal. The gods, the Viśve-devas, and all the world bow before a transformation that has arrived."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca yasyāṅgirā vṛddhatamaḥ pitāmaho; bṛhaspatiś cāpi pitā tapodhanaḥ ṛṣeḥ putraṃ tam atho vāpi pautraṃ; kathaṃ na śoceyam ahaṃ na rudyām
english: Devayānī said: "He whose grandfather is the most venerable Āṅgiras, and whose father too is the ascetic-wealthy Bṛhaspati — how should I not grieve, how should I not weep for the son or even the grandson of such a sage?"

sanskrit: sa brahmacārī ca tapodhanaś ca; sadotthitaḥ karmasu caiva dakṣaḥ kacasya mārgaṃ pratipatsye na bhokṣye; priyo hi me tāta kaco 'bhirūpaḥ
english: "He was a celibate student, rich in austerity, ever diligent and skilled in his duties. Father, I shall follow the path of Kaca — I will not eat; for dear to me is the handsome Kaca."

sanskrit: śukra uvāca asaṃśayaṃ mām asurā dviṣanti; ye me śiṣyaṃ nāgasaṃ sūdayanti abrāhmaṇaṃ kartum icchanti raudrās; te māṃ yathā prastutaṃ dānavair hi apy asya pāpasya bhaved ihāntaḥ; kaṃ brahmahatyā na dahed apīndram
english: Śukra said: "Without doubt the demons hate me — these terrible ones who slay my blameless pupil and wish to make me a non-brahmin; they act toward me as demons have plotted. But there would be an end to this evil here; what person would the guilt of brahmin-slaughter not burn, even Indra himself?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saṃcodito devayānyā maharṣiḥ punar āhvayat saṃrambheṇaiva kāvyo hi bṛhaspatisutaṃ kacam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Urged by Devayānī, the great sage Kāvya called out to Bṛhaspati's son Kaca once more, with great intensity."

sanskrit: guror bhīto vidyayā copahūtaḥ; śanair vācaṃ jaṭhare vyājahāra tam abravīt kena pathopanīto; mamodare tiṣṭhasi brūhi vipra
english: Summoned by the teacher's knowledge and speaking from fear of his guru, a faint voice arose from within the belly. He said to him: "Tell me, brahmin — by what path have you entered, and how do you remain in my belly?"

sanskrit: kaca uvāca bhavatprasādān na jahāti māṃ smṛtiḥ; smare ca sarvaṃ yac ca yathā ca vṛttam na tv evaṃ syāt tapaso vyayo me; tataḥ kleśaṃ ghoram imaṃ sahāmi
english: Kaca said: "By your grace, memory does not leave me; I remember everything — what happened and how. But it should not be that there is a waste of my austerity; and so I endure this terrible suffering."

sanskrit: asuraiḥ surāyāṃ bhavato 'smi datto; hatvā dagdhvā cūrṇayitvā ca kāvya brāhmīṃ māyām āsurī caiva māyā; tvayi sthite katham evātivartet
english: "I was given to you in wine by the demons, O Kāvya, after they slew, burned, and ground me to powder. How could the demonic magic ever prevail against the divine magic while you stand firm?"

sanskrit: śukra uvāca kiṃ te priyaṃ karavāṇy adya vatse; vadhena me jīvitaṃ syāt kacasya nānyatra kukṣer mama bhedanena; dṛśyet kaco madgato devayāni
english: Śukra said: "What shall I do that is pleasing to you today, my son? Kaca could live only at the cost of my death — for Kaca who is inside me, O Devayānī, could be seen only by splitting my belly."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca dvau māṃ śokāv agnikalpau dahetāṃ; kacasya nāśas tava caivopaghātaḥ kacasya nāśe mama nāsti śarma; tavopaghāte jīvituṃ nāsmi śaktā
english: Devayānī said: "Two griefs, like fire, would burn me: the destruction of Kaca and harm to you. In the destruction of Kaca there is no peace for me; yet if you are harmed I am unable to live."

sanskrit: śukra uvāca saṃsiddharūpo 'si bṛhaspateḥ suta; yat tvāṃ bhaktaṃ bhajate devayānī vidyām imāṃ prāpnuhi jīvanīṃ tvaṃ; na ced indraḥ kacarūpī tvam adya
english: Śukra said: "You are fully accomplished in form, O son of Bṛhaspati, since the devoted Devayānī cherishes you. Receive this life-restoring knowledge — for if you were not Kaca today, you would be Indra himself in that form."

sanskrit: na nivartet punar jīvan kaś cid anyo mamodarāt brāhmaṇaṃ varjayitvaikaṃ tasmād vidyām avāpnuhi
english: "No one else living would return again from my belly — except a brahmin alone; therefore receive the knowledge."

sanskrit: putro bhūtvā bhāvaya bhāvito mām; asmād dehād upaniṣkramya tāta samīkṣethā dharmavatīm avekṣāṃ; guroḥ sakāśāt prāpya vidyāṃ savidyaḥ
english: "Becoming my son, sustain me who have sustained you; emerging from this body, my son, consider the righteous regard I have for you — and having received the knowledge from your teacher, be endowed with knowledge."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca guroḥ sakāśāt samavāpya vidyāṃ; bhittvā kukṣiṃ nirvicakrāma vipraḥ kaco 'bhirūpo dakṣiṇaṃ brāhmaṇasya; śuklātyaye paurṇamāsyām ivenduḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Having received the knowledge from his teacher, the handsome brahmin Kaca burst through the belly and came forth on the right side of the brahmin — like the moon on a full-moon night at the close of the bright fortnight."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ patitaṃ brahmarāśim; utthāpayām āsa mṛtaṃ kaco 'pi vidyāṃ siddhāṃ tām avāpyābhivādya; tataḥ kacas taṃ gurum ity uvāca
english: And seeing that mass of brahmic splendor fallen, Kaca himself raised up the dead man. Having obtained that accomplished knowledge and having paid obeisance, Kaca then addressed him as teacher.

sanskrit: ṛtasya dātāram anuttamasya; nidhiṃ nidhīnāṃ caturanvayānām ye nādriyante gurum arcanīyaṃ; pāpāṃl lokāṃs te vrajanty apratiṣṭhān
english: "Those who do not revere the teacher who is worthy of worship — the giver of the highest truth, the treasury of treasuries through four lineages — they go to sinful worlds without foundation."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca surāpānād vañcanāṃ prāpayitvā; saṃjñānāśaṃ caiva tathātighoram dṛṣṭvā kacaṃ cāpi tathābhirūpaṃ; pītaṃ tadā surayā mohitena
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Having brought about deception through the drinking of wine and the destruction of consciousness so terrible, and having seen Kaca who had been swallowed in wine by one who was deluded and who was also so handsome —"

sanskrit: samanyur utthāya mahānubhāvas; tadośanā viprahitaṃ cikīrṣuḥ kāvyaḥ svayaṃ vākyam idaṃ jagāda; surāpānaṃ prati vai jātaśaṅkaḥ
english: "— the great-souled one rose up in anger; Uśanas Kāvya himself, wishing to do what was good for brahmins and now deeply troubled about wine-drinking, spoke these words:"

sanskrit: yo brāhmaṇo 'dya prabhṛtīha kaś cin; mohāt surāṃ pāsyati mandabuddhiḥ apetadharmo brahmahā caiva sa syād; asmiṃl loke garhitaḥ syāt pare ca
english: "Whatever brahmin henceforth in this world, dull-witted, drinks wine out of delusion — he becomes one fallen from righteousness and also a slayer of brahmins; he shall be censured in this world and in the next."

sanskrit: mayā cemāṃ vipradharmoktisīmāṃ; maryādāṃ vai sthāpitāṃ sarvaloke santo viprāḥ śuśruvāṃso gurūṇāṃ; devā lokāś copaśṛṇvantu sarve
english: "And this boundary of brahminical law that I have established throughout all the world — let the virtuous brahmins who hearken to their teachers, and let all the gods and all the worlds, hear it."

sanskrit: itīdam uktvā sa mahānubhāvas; taponidhīnāṃ nidhir aprameyaḥ tān dānavān daivavimūḍhabuddhīn; idaṃ samāhūya vaco 'bhyuvāca
english: Having spoken thus, that great-souled one — the immeasurable treasury of all treasuries of austerity — summoned those demons whose minds were blinded by fate, and spoke these words to them.

sanskrit: ācakṣe vo dānavā bāliśāḥ stha; siddhaḥ kaco vatsyati matsakāśe saṃjīvanīṃ prāpya vidyāṃ mahārthāṃ; tulyaprabhāvo brahmaṇā brahmabhūtaḥ
english: "I declare to you — you demons are foolish. Kaca has succeeded and shall remain with me; having obtained the life-restoring knowledge of great import, he is equal in splendor to Brahman and has become Brahman-natured."

sanskrit: guror uṣya sakāśe tu daśa varṣaśatāni saḥ anujñātaḥ kaco gantum iyeṣa tridaśālayam
english: Having dwelt near his teacher for a thousand years, Kaca, given leave to depart, desired to go to the abode of the thirty gods.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca samāvṛttavrataṃ taṃ tu visṛṣṭaṃ guruṇā tadā prasthitaṃ tridaśāvāsaṃ devayāny abravīd idam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "But as he, his vow completed and released by the teacher, set out toward the dwelling of the thirty gods, Devayānī said this to him."

sanskrit: ṛṣer aṅgirasaḥ pautra vṛttenābhijanena ca bhrājase vidyayā caiva tapasā ca damena ca
english: "O grandson of the sage Āṅgiras, you shine by your conduct and birth, and also by knowledge, austerity, and self-restraint."

sanskrit: ṛṣir yathāṅgirā mānyaḥ pitur mama mahāyaśāḥ tathā mānyaś ca pūjyaś ca bhūyo mama bṛhaspatiḥ
english: "Just as the sage Āṅgiras is revered and of great renown to my father, so too is Bṛhaspati to me — worthy of reverence and worship above all."

sanskrit: evaṃ jñātvā vijānīhi yad bravīmi tapodhana vratasthe niyamopete yathā vartāmy ahaṃ tvayi
english: "Knowing this, understand what I say to you, O ascetic-wealthy one — understand how I have conducted myself toward you while you were engaged in your vow and observances."

sanskrit: sa samāvṛttavidyo māṃ bhaktāṃ bhajitum arhasi gṛhāṇa pāṇiṃ vidhivan mama mantrapuraskṛtam
english: "You, now returned with your knowledge, should favor me who am devoted to you; take my hand in the proper manner, with sacred mantras duly preceding."

sanskrit: kaca uvāca pūjyo mānyaś ca bhagavān yathā tava pitā mama tathā tvam anavadyāṅgi pūjanīyatarā mama
english: Kaca said: "Just as your venerable father is to be worshipped and revered by me, so too are you, O blameless-limbed one — even more deserving of my veneration."
